deck: CS3357A Networks::Quiz 1 Review::Slide numbers - which is which

fields.Front: Which access technology do the slides quote at 24–52 Mbps downstream and 3.5–16 Mbps upstream?
fields.Back: DSL, on a dedicated line to the central office DSLAM (slide 28).

fields.Front: Which access technology do the slides quote at 40 Mbps–1.2 Gbps downstream and 30–100 Mbps upstream?
fields.Back: Cable (HFC): asymmetric, shared to the cable headend / CMTS (slide 30).

fields.Front: Which link type do the slides give as "up to 45 Mbps per channel, 270 msec end-end delay"?
fields.Back: Satellite (geosynchronous vs low-earth-orbit), slide 37. Terrestrial microwave is also "up to 45 Mbps channels" but has no 270 ms figure.

fields.Front: Which slide technologies are quoted at 11, 54, 450 Mbps?
fields.Back: WiFi (802.11b/g/n) WLAN access points, in home, wireless and enterprise networks (slides 31–33).

fields.Front: What range do the slides give for a WLAN and for wide-area cellular?
fields.Back: WLAN: ~100 ft (within or around a building). Cellular: 10's of km at 10's of Mbps (slide 32).

fields.Text: Twisted pair: Category 5 = {{c1::100 Mbps, 1 Gbps}} Ethernet; Category 6 = {{c1::10 Gbps}} Ethernet. Enterprise Ethernet on the slides: {{c1::100 Mbps, 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps}}; home wired Ethernet: {{c1::1 Gbps}}.

fields.Front: Which medium is described as "two concentric copper conductors, bidirectional, broadband, 100's Mbps per channel"?
Which medium carries "light pulses, each pulse a bit" at 10's–100's Gbps?
fields.Back: Fiber optic cable (slide 36): low error rate, repeaters spaced far apart, immune to electromagnetic noise.

fields.Front: What are the three propagation-environment effects on wireless radio listed on slide 37, and what are its two transmission properties?
fields.Back: Effects: reflection, obstruction by objects, interference. Properties: broadcast and half-duplex (sender to receiver), with no physical wire.

fields.Front: Slide 43 circuit-switching diagram: how many circuits per link, and which circuits does the call get?
fields.Back: Each link has four circuits. The call gets the 2nd circuit in the top link and the 1st circuit in the right link.

fields.Front: Slide 55: name the four tier-1 ISPs and the content providers given as examples.
fields.Back: Tier-1: Level 3, Sprint, AT&T, NTT. Content providers: Google, Facebook (slide 55); Google, Microsoft, Akamai (slide 54).

fields.Front: Slide 58: what does nodal processing do, and how long does it typically take?
fields.Back: It checks bit errors and determines the output link. Typically < msec.
